paragraphs.text: Gopeed downloader tools for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): add / list / status / control / process / launch
, plus a background job that wakes an idle agent. Agents: read docs/AGENTS.md first.
dsh-gopeed-downloader
English | Chinese
7 tools  |  HTTP, magnet and .torrent URLs  |  process control Windows-only  |  needs Gopeed 1.9.3+

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reading this as an agent? Stop and open docs/AGENTS.md instead.**
>
> That file i

s the contract: the seven tools with the result fields DSH validates, the **do-not-poll** rule
> for
`gopeed_add`, the save-location order, an error playbook keyed on `verdict`, and an explicit do-not

> list. This README is the human landing page and deliberately does not repeat it.
>
> **If you mai
ntain an agent that uses this plugin, point it at that URL -- not at this file.**

Turn a local **Gopeed** download manager into agent tools inside **DeepSeek Harness
(DSH)**: start d

ownloads, follow them, steer them, diagnose or launch the Gopeed process, and receive
download-compl
ete events -- including a background job that wakes an idle agent.
Any link Gopeed itself accepts works: **HTTP/HTTPS direct links**, **magnet links** and **remote `.t

orrent`
URLs**. A local `.torrent` file is not accepted -- there is no upload path, so hand over the

URL it came
from instead. BitTorrent detail (peers, DHT, trackers, seeding) stays with Gopeed; the

plugin creates the task
and reads its progress, nothing more.
The agent hands a URL to Gopeed over its loopback HTTP endpoint; Gopeed owns the outbound traffic an

d the
files on disk, so nothing passes through the model or a shell. Gopeed's desktop build listens

on a random port
per launch by default, so the plugin reads the live port from the running process (

`port: 0`) unless you pin
one. See Configuration.
## What it does
| Goal | Tool |
| Start a download and be told when it ends | `gopeed_add` -- takes a direct link, a magnet link or
a remote `.torrent` URL, and returns a background job; the completion notice is DSH's own, so a busy

agent reads it next step and an idle agent is woken. |
| Watch progress | `gopeed_list`, `gopeed_st

atus` -- one flat task shape (`percent`, `sizeKnown`, speed, real save directory). |
| Steer a downl
oad | `gopeed_control` -- pause / resume / remove through an `action` enum. `remove` deletes the fil

es too unless `force: false`. |
| Fix the setup | `gopeed_process` -- one of six verdicts plus pid,

memory, version, executable path and webhook status. |
| Start a stopped Gopeed | `gopeed_launch` --

the agent-side equivalent of double-clicking the icon. |
| Hear downloads finish | `gopeed_events`
-- reads the `DOWNLOAD_DONE` / `DOWNLOAD_ERROR` pushes Gopeed sent; `action: "apply"` saves the webh
ook address into Gopeed's config in `auto` mode. |
## What it does not do
- **No tool can restart or kill Gopeed.** Restarting is the red **Restart Gopeed** button on the plu

gin
settings page, a user action, because it interrupts downloads in flight. `gopeed_launch` only st

arts an
absent process and has no parameters.
- **Process control is Windows-only.** `gopeed_process

`, `gopeed_launch`, the restart button and executable
auto-discovery all call Windows tools. The dow

nload tools work wherever Gopeed runs.
- **The webhook listener binds `127.0.0.1` only.** A Gopeed i

n Docker or on another machine cannot push to it
without extra networking; poll `gopeed_list` / `gop

eed_status` instead.
- **The plugin never writes into the conversation.** No user-role messages, no

forged follow-ups; guidance
rides inside a tool's own result.
## Requirements

- **DSH**, running, with a profile that can install bundles (the `plugin_manager` tool, or the Web
*

*Plugins** page).
- **Gopeed 1.9.3 or newer**, reachable on `host:port`. Verified against 1.9.3.
- *
*No Node.js, npm or pnpm is needed to run this plugin.** It is a Cordis plugin inside the DSH host p

rocess
and never shells out to a package manager.
- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 is enough** -- the proc

ess helpers only use `tasklist`, `taskkill`,
`powershell.exe`, `netstat` and `netsh`.
## Installation
`dsh-gopeed-downloader` is on npm. In any DSH session, tell the agent:
> Install the `dsh-gopeed-downloader` bundle from npm.
That is `plugin_manager` with `action: "install_bundle"` and `target: "dsh-gopeed-downloader"`. DSH

installs it
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations
1. **A forced restart interrupts downloads.** That is why it is a user-triggered button and not a to

ol. The
failure paths are reported by stage; the success path must not be expected to preserve in-fl

ight progress.
2. **Webhook delivery depends on Gopeed applying its config after a full restart.** U

ntil then the GUI may show
stale values, and no event will arrive. The plugin cannot tell "not enabl

ed in Gopeed" apart from "enabled
but not restarted"; both look like zero events received.
3. **Even

ts are in-memory.** The ring buffer holds 50 entries and is emptied by a plugin reload or a DSH
rest

art. Nothing is written to disk.
4. **The settings form's visual layout is unverified.** The data pa

th (slot key, `form.state` / `mutate`,
field projection, token redaction) is tested; the styling is

inline CSS nobody has looked at in a browser.
5. **BT / magnet tasks are lightly tested.** A Debian

13.7 netinst ISO magnet was verified end to end (metadata
resolved to 756 MB, about 4 MB/s, tracking

job followed it). Harder cases -- a magnet with no peers, DHT-only
discovery, a private tracker, re

suming a magnet after a restart -- are unverified. A missing `meta.res`
degrades to `sizeKnown: fals

e` rather than an invented percentage.
6. **`remove` is idempotent.** Gopeed 1.9.3 answers a `DELETE

` for an unknown id with success, so deleting
twice still reports "removed".
7. **Readiness after a

restart is inferred by polling the endpoint,** so a Gopeed that already serves requests
while still

showing a loading screen is reported ready early. Harmless.
8. **The webhook listener binds loopback

only.** A Gopeed running in Docker, or on another machine, cannot push
to it without extra networki

ng.
9. **Download tracking does not survive a DSH restart.** A tracking job lives in the DSH process

, so restarting
DSH (or upgrading the plugin) drops every tracker; the downloads themselves continue

inside Gopeed and stay
visible to `gopeed_status`. There is no persistence and no re-attach. A plug

in reload at least reports the
loss: each live tracker settles as `killed` with a detail saying the

download state is unknown.
[该节后续省略]
